# Aeneid — questions for the owner

Open:

1. **Approve the pilot?** aeneid-001 (I.1–101) is live. If approved, add `aeneid` to `.github/pipeline/queue.txt`
   (after `beowulf`, or wherever you want it) and the shared routine continues the poem from aeneid-002.
2. **Edition: Greenough (1881), not Hirtzel (1900).** Hirtzel could not be fetched (no reachable machine-readable
   copy). Greenough is the Perseus text and public domain. Meanwhile: proceeding on Greenough. Switching later means
   re-archiving and re-issuing published parts.
3. **Audio for the pilot.** Pushing a new Latin part does not build its audio; the daily sweep reaches the Aeneid only
   after the Odyssey, Igor, Aesop and all of Ovid (none of Ovid has audio yet either). A single *Build audio* dispatch
   with id `aeneid-001` would make it now (≈35k characters of SSML plus word clips; inside the $10/month budget).
   Meanwhile: left to the sweep.
4. **Library sub-grouping.** Aeneid entries carry `group: "Book I"` etc. (as the Odyssey does), so once there are
   several parts the text picker shows them under book headings. Ovid's entries have none. Meanwhile: kept.
5. **Dido's suicide (Book IV)** is not covered by any content-advisory trigger (the same gap noted for Ovid).
   Meanwhile: no advisory unless a trigger fires; to be decided before aeneid-030 (IV.607–705), where her death falls.

6. **I.203 set piece decided by the run.** The conventions asked for a dedicated pass before the batch reaching I.203; the unattended run built it from the Latin, rephrased away from known versions, and recorded it in the house-renderings table. Meanwhile: published as is; change it if you prefer another.
7. **Glossary `genitor`.** The broadened entry keeps the old "here Neptune" reading whole, per the broadening rule; the new reading (Jupiter, voc.) is appended.

8. **I.462 set piece decided by the run (aeneid-005).** As with I.203 (item 6): built from the Latin alone, rephrased away from known versions, added to the house-renderings table. The reviewer could only check against remembered versions. Meanwhile: published as is; change it if you prefer another.

The last two could be rule-5 source fixes with a re-pin of aeneid-069, but the printed page could not be checked (as 8.137, 9.289); confirm the marks and they can be added. Doubtful quantity on the only fit: 9.584 *Sȳmaethia*. Left as the scanner gives them, consistent with published parts: syllable division in `ad-` compounds (561 `adripit`, 578 `adlapsa`). Unchecked attributions from memory: Iliad 12 as general model of the wall fight; Iliad 12.41–48 (beast killed by its own courage), 22.308–310 (eagle seizing lamb or hare), 2.235 (Thersites, "Achaean women"); sling-bullets melting in flight; raiding as honourable in early Italy; *vetitis armis* as a slave's son barred from service (noted as "perhaps"). Meanwhile: published as is.

64. **Misprints, a metrical reading and scansion (aeneid-070).** Treated as misprints under rule 5b (t as printed, l/i corrected, note opens with the print's reading): 9.635 `His capti Phryges` for `Bis` (Ascanius throws Numanus's *bis capti Phryges*, 599, back at him; Latin Library `bis`); 9.644 `capit. ”Simul` and 9.656 `bello. ”Sic` (closing mark joined to the next word, as 8.404, 9.22) — here the stray ” stands at the start of the next unit's t and l/i close the speech on the earlier unit (042's handling), because carrying the narrative on would make six-line units; 9.654 `magnus, Apollo` (stray comma: Apollo names himself, no vocative; as 6.844, 7.170); 9.683 lowercase `inrumpunt` after a full stop (item 43 still open). Kept as printed: 9.676 `animis` (LL `armis`), 9.686 `at` (LL `aut`). **9.646** *Forma tum vertitur oris*: the reviewer made *formā* ablative of respect with Apollo as subject, because nominative *forma* cannot scan there; say if you read it otherwise. Doubtful quantities on the only fit: 9.653 *Aenīdē*, 9.680 *Ăthĕsim*, 9.673 *Ĭaera* (three syllables). Glossary: *commissa* still lacks "entrusted" (675); its entry is already over 230 characters, so it could not be broadened — rule whether to shorten it. Unchecked attributions from memory: Iliad 1.528, 17.322–325, 1.46, 12.131–134, 12.156–158, 4.504, 2.783; Georgics 1.40; Eclogue 3.87; Thebe in the Troad; Roman piers at Baiae. Meanwhile: published as is.
